clue.text: Pacifier put to mouth, say, almost having this effect?

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or placate

indicators.note: almost means the word is taken short of its final letter

parts.note: a mouth is an example of an orifice, 'say' marking the example

explanation.surface: A baby's dummy put in its mouth nearly sends it off to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ORIFICE to ORIFIC. The question mark flags that the clue's own picture, a sop that soothes, illustrates the sleep-inducing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soporific induces sleep, which is the effect a soothing pacifier has on a baby.

clue.text: Lock phosphorus in part of plant

indicators.note: in means the symbol is placed inside the word for lock

parts.note: to lock is to seal shut
p is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: Locking phosphorus up inside a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like parts of a flower's calyx, protecting the bud.

clue.text: I don't believe you fancy a different cracker

definitions.meaning: a colloquial retort meaning you are teasing me
a Christmas cracker is pulled by two people, so you might pull the second one

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses disbelief, from pulling someone's leg; literally it invites pulling another cracker.

clue.text: Warning — such a district is vicious

definitions.meaning: a signal of danger telling you to stop
a district of brothels, full of vice

explanation.definitionFit: A red signal warns of danger, and the red-light district is where prostitution and vice are found.

clue.text: Over-subtle penalties applied to feature of some of our clues

parts.note: fines are penalties

parts.words: feature of some of our clues
parts.note: puns are wordplay found in many cryptic clues

explanation.surface: Penalties are imposed for the over-clever wordplay in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fine-spun is spun so delicately as to be overly subtle or elaborate.

clue.text: Takes the best biscuits

definitions.meaning: to cream off is to take the best part
cream crackers, or biscuits sandwiched with cream

explanation.definitionFit: To cream is to skim off the finest portion; creams are also cream-filled biscuits.

clue.text: Poet's lost his third watch

indicators.note: the poet's name loses its third letter, which is the R

parts.note: Virgil is the Roman poet of the Aeneid; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A poet has mislaid his third wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of keeping watch, especially through the night.

clue.text: Check cover, if you're included

indicators.note: included signals that the answer lies within the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: Confirm your insurance policy includes you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' points to the letters running across coVER IF You're.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify is to check that something is true or accurate.

clue.text: More yielded by villages in this Islamic uprising?

definitions.text: More yielded by villages in this Islamic uprising?

parts.words: More yielded by villages in this Islamic uprising?
parts.note: the agricultural transformation of crop yields in rural areas, punningly read as a revolt under the colour of Islam

explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s programme of high-yield crops boosted harvests in developing countries; green is also Islam's colour.

clue.text: Doubly dead language?

parts.note: a classical language is already dead, and late also means deceased, so it is dead twice

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin of late antiquity is a dead language, and 'late' can mean deceased, hence doubly dead.

clue.text: Champion youth in agony

indicators.note: in means the youth's word sits inside the word for agony

parts.note: pain is agony
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A young sporting champion is suffering terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin was one of Charlemagne's knights, hence a heroic champion of a cause.

clue.text: Head gets to heart of most stingy pledge

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for most stingy moves into its middle

parts.note: near means mean or stingy, so the most stingy is nearest

explanation.surface: A boss reaches the core of the meanest promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head gets to heart of' takes the leading N of NEAREST and moves it to the middle, giving EAR-N-EST.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest is a token payment given as a pledge that a bargain will be kept.

clue.text: Strip of wood I used for police weapon

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood

explanation.surface: A slat of timber is used by the police as a truncheon.
explanation.walkthrough: A LATHI is the long iron-bound stick carried by police in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The lathi is the heavy bamboo baton used by Indian police for crowd control.

clue.text: Tie is provided with very important clothing

indicators.note: clothing means the very-important word wraps around the word for provided

parts.note: seminal means highly influential or very important
if means provided, as in 'provided that'

explanation.surface: A necktie comes with vital garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' looks like the neckwear, given the clothing; it is a cup tie, a match in a knockout competition.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a tie is a knockout match, and a semifinal is one such match before the final.

clue.text: Substantiate vegetarian slogan.

definitions.meaning: to add detail and substance to an outline
read as a protest cry demanding that meat be got rid of

explanation.definitionFit: To flesh out a plan is to give it substance; read literally the phrase banishes meat.

clue.text: One protecting catch in port?

definitions.meaning: a guardian of the fish caught
a ferry port in Pembrokeshire, west Wales

explanation.definitionFit: Fishguard is a Welsh harbour town, and read literally it names a watcher over fish.

clue.text: Run fast and fall hard

definitions.meaning: to ... along is to run at speed
rain is said to ... down when it falls heavily

explanation.definitionFit: Pelt means both to hurry along at speed and, of rain, to pour down heavily.

clue.text: Provide pretty good coverage for the present

definitions.text: Provide pretty good coverage for the present

parts.words: Provide pretty good coverage for the present
parts.note: seems to mean adequate cover for now, but means covering a gift attractively

explanation.definitionFit: To wrap a gift in decorative paper is to give a present pretty coverage.

clue.text: Serviceman able to sing I found among members of cavalry

indicators.note: the I is set among the letters, the members, of the following word and all rearranged

explanation.surface: A singing soldier serves in a cavalry regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found among members of' mixes I with the letters of CAVALRY. A LAY VICAR is a lay singer in a cathedral choir, taking part in services.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay vicar is a layman who sings in cathedral services, a singer serving the church.

clue.text: Provide more than enough, so seconds consumed

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Someone over-caters, so the second helpings got eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To glut someone, supplying more than they want, is to satisfy them completely.

clue.text: Old dance first to be cut from musical

indicators.note: the opening letter is removed from the musical's title

parts.note: Brigadoon is a Lerner and Loewe stage musical about a vanishing Scottish village

explanation.surface: An old dance number has been dropped from a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigadoon is a lively Provençal dance for couples, popular in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Continued to be imperturbable while speaking

indicators.note: while speaking signals the word for imperturbable is pronounced, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: staid means sober and unflappable

explanation.surface: Someone carried on calmly while giving a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed is to have remained or continued in place.

clue.text: In his heart, ambassador intends to be consistent

indicators.note: In means the ambassador's letters go inside the word for heart

parts.note: the core is the heart of something
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An ambassador privately means to be reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, the formal title of an ambassador; 'his' and 'intends' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together logically, being consistent.

clue.text: One may cover officer needing a car to get out

indicators.note: out signals that these letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An army officer needs a car to get out of the barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of A CAR TO GET.
explanation.definitionFit: A greatcoat is a heavy military overcoat, worn by an officer over the uniform.

clue.text: Boast verse is written by relative

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A family member writes poetry to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaunt is to boast or brag about something.

clue.text: Italian poet a fool, breaking good books up

indicators.note: breaking means the fool splits the reversed books apart
up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An Italian poet is an idiot who smashes up the sacred texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OT to TO, and ASS breaks into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the 16th-century Italian poet of Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Relieving hurt unit of force, a number being at the front

parts.note: a dyne is the unit of force in the centimetre-gram-second system

explanation.surface: A soothing balm, measured in force units, puts a number first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being at the front' tells you the article and the number come before the unit of force, although the clue mentions them after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a painkiller, so as an adjective it means pain-relieving.

clue.text: Chain that's covered in diamonds

indicators.note: covered in means the abbreviation for that is sits inside the word for diamonds

parts.note: rocks is slang for diamonds
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A necklace encrusted with precious gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chain' looks like a necklace of diamonds; it is a mountain range in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rockies are a long chain of mountains running through western North America.

clue.text: Daughter's study a fright

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for daughter
to read a subject is to study it, especially at university

explanation.surface: A girl's academic course causes her terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear, a synonym of fright.

clue.text: In agitation, present a ring, making special speech

indicators.note: agitation means stirring up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: o looks like a ring

explanation.surface: Nervously, a suitor offers a ring with a special speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In agitation' acts on the two words that follow it, and the ring is added afterwards, outside the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an artificial international language, a specially invented form of speech.
